correctness.rationale: The exact Laplacian path eigendecomposition, odd-residue permutation and paired sine-product give the node-independent product of squared eigenvector coordinates. The Vandermonde factor and triangular unit endpoint Kalman matrix prove integer determinant 0 or +/-1. Modal factorization against an L2 Gram matrix of distinct exponentials proves the all-T determinant formula and positivity, including the undamped constant mode for finite T. Counting reduced odd residue classes gives phi(2n). An exact-symbolic n=2..18 checker and high-precision/physical-coordinate numerical checks (602 assertions) all passed; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2011 path-reachability theorem already supplies the arithmetic controllability criterion, which is explicitly excluded from novelty. The inspected paper gives no Kalman determinant +/-1 result and no quantitative finite-horizon Gramian-volume classification. The 2013 actuator placement paper develops the trace Gramian metric, not the determinant identity. The closest full published result on normalized-path dynamical sampling gives generically endpoint-optimal determinants for a *different degree-normalized operator* and does not entail the all-location ties proved here on dyadic combinatorial-Laplacian paths. The new contribution is the unimodular integer classification and all-horizon D-optimal equality. These are not deduced from the cited prior claims without the new universal cosine-product comparison and endpoint determinant argument. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent or straightforward unpublished corollaries remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent Kalman-unimodularity or finite-horizon Gramian-volume identity could predate this work.
The result is derivable from standard path spectral formulas plus a nontrivial cosine-product identity; novelty is in the quantitative universal invariant, not the published reachability criterion.
No claim is made for degree-normalized path systems, where a closely related published result gives a different ordering.

value.rationale: The attainable-control-volume determinant is a standard natural actuator-placement objective. On ordinary paths, exact unimodularity classifies every single input over infinitely many sizes and proves a previously non-obvious horizon- and damping-universal D-optimal degeneracy: all n vertices tie on dyadic paths, despite degree disparities and unequal small-time trace objectives. This sharp structural identity is meaningful for comparing actuator design metrics and exact arithmetic controllability, not a renamed rank condition or arbitrary parameter slice. Limits to unit paths and a single actuator are explicit.
